- Defense control vs shared control for technical responses
- OSS and training-data carveouts

Can we schedule a short kickoff with your legal/ops folks to go through a concession ladder — what we can reasonably offer now vs items that require exec approval? Ideally later this week or early next.

Subject: Re: Request: IP indemnity concessions for MSA/Order Form

Emma — thanks for sending the redlines and for the context.

Quick read: the asks are within the typical range but there are 3 areas where we should be explicit on our fallback positions and approval path:

1) Defense control: Redwood's standard is to retain the right to defend with cooperation; we can offer shared technical response rights for SaaS-only deployments if LongWave provides a named liaison and an agreed evidence escrow threshold.

2) Cap: we can tolerate a percentage-based cap tied to annualized committed spend for Dedicated or Private deals. For pure hosted pay-as-you-go customers, we will propose a scaled cap (e.g., 1x ARR of the prior 12 months or a fixed multiple of average monthly spend) — needs procurement signoff.

3) OSS/training data carveouts: we generally carve out known OSS and public-domain training artifacts, but we will need a schedule for any negotiated carveouts.

I've attached an internal concession matrix (internal_concession_matrix.xlsx) with suggested tiers: "standard" (self-service customers), "committed" (reserved capacity), and "enterprise" (Dedicated/Private). Laura — can you review the matrix and flag any commercial items that Procurement will need to route to FP&A/Finance for cap modeling?

Emma — proposing a 30-minute call Friday 11/21 at 10:00am PT to walk the ladder and identify must-haves vs nice-to-haves. If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: IP indemnity concessions for MSA/Order Form

Markus / Laura — quick legal take ahead of the Friday call. I'm pasting high-level positions so we go into the kickoff aligned.

- Defense & Control: our preferred rule is "Redwood defends, customer cooperates". Offer shared control only for non-litigation technical responses (e.g., triage, takedown support). We should NOT cede overall settlement authority unless we get insurable indemnity or an escrow/insurance offset.

- Notice window & cure: propose a 60-day notice + 30-day technical cure where applicable. Shorter windows (30 days) are risky operationally.

- Cap design: tie to committed spend where possible. For enterprise (Dedicated/Private) consider a tiered cap: 1x ARR for first-party claims, 3x ARR for third-party infringement only under narrow conditions. For hosted customers with low ARR, consider a floor (e.g., $250k) so we don't have disproportionate unlimited exposure.

- OSS & training-data carveouts: explicitly exclude claims arising solely from widely-available OSS licensed under standard permissive licenses; require customer to provide a list of any proprietary datasets they supply that trigger carveouts.

- Insurance & escrow: if customer requests defend-and-control we should request evidence of insurance limits and consider escrow or an insurance-backed holdback for very large exposure.

Laura — can you confirm whether FP&A can run the 1x/3x cap scenarios for DW-7834 before Friday? If not, we'll call out the options as conditional and ask for an exec approval lane.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@longwave.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 14:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: IP indemnity concessions for MSA/Order Form — proposed lane

Emma — thanks for the patience. Quick recap and proposed lane for LongWave (so we have something to discuss on the call):

1) Defense control: Redwood will lead defense; we will provide a named technical liaison to coordinate triage with LongWave. For litigation-level decisions we reserve settlement authority unless an insurance-backed holdback (or exec approval) is in place.

2) Cap: For DW-7834 we propose a tiered cap tied to committed spend: 1x committed ARR for Redwood-hosted services; for Dedicated/Private add-on we can discuss a 3x ARR limit for third-party IP under narrow conditions. If LongWave prefers a fixed-dollar cap instead, propose a $500k floor.

3) Notice & cure: 60 days notice, 30 days technical cure for triage and mitigation.

4) OSS & training data: carve out claims solely attributable to widely-licensed OSS or public-domain datasets. Require LongWave to supply any proprietary-supplied training data lists for carveout validation.

Next steps:
- Laura / FP&A to confirm ARR modeling for DW-7834 so we can pick the appropriate cap bracket.
- Markus to send a marked-up MSA/Order Form with the concession ladder (I will circulate tonight).
- Emma to confirm Friday 10:00am PT/alternate time if the 11/21 slot still works for you — if so I'll send a calendar invite and a tentative agenda (30m).

Attachment: proposal_for_longwave_v1.docx (docx)

Thanks all — looking forward to resolving this quickly.

Markus
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
